item.title: Top 5 Methods to Retrieve Query Parameters from a URL
item.description:
Given a URL like /some_path?some_key=some_value, how can developers efficiently extract the value of query parameters in Python? If you are using Django and initially tried using self.request.get('some_key') but it didn’t yield the expected results, you might find the following approaches useful.

Method 1: Using Django’s Built-in Method

A common and effective method to access query parameters in Django is by leveraging the request.GET attribute. The implementation is straightforward:

def my_view(request):
    some_value = request.GET.get('some_key')
    return HttpResponse(f'The value of some_key is: {some_value}')

This approach fetches the value associated with some_key, returning None if the key doesn’t exist in the query string.
